title: Opus 5.5 one-shot this trailer for me in about 40 minutes
author: dreamswedontshare
selftext:
I had the music available, everything else is Opus while I ate my lunch. 

TL;DR: Forgot to push my actual project to git before leaving home for two days, so decided to create a fun little game to keep me occupied, and asked Claude Code to create a trailer for it.

Long version:

Of course, the video is far from perfect, but the prompt was the one-shottiest of them all, so I'd feel bad if I wanted more out of it.

There was a very good post here yesterday about how Opus can create great pixel art scenes, I just can't find it sadly, but credits to that dude! (Will update if I manage to find it)

I copied the prompt OP posted there, adjusted it, and sent it to both Astra and Opus. Astra was great with it, too, but I liked Opus' approach more so I told Claude to gamify it. At first just wanted to one-shot a playable game level, but it was kind of fun and since I forgot to bring my project with me to my retreat, I went with it. 

Wrote some light lore, figured out some mechanics, and spent about 12-16 hours with it on Opus 5.5 medium/high on a 100 dollar plan up until now. There were a couple five hour sessions where Claude was non-stop active, but I couldn't reach my 5 hour limit once (got to like 56% once I think). My weekly limit is at 34% used right now, which coming from Astra is mind-blowing in itself. Sure, its a very easy little project, but I know Codex would have eaten up most of my 20x weekly limit with it.

Opus made the visuals and the ingame audio, and right now there is a decent bit of content. 

The player fights through a forest at first, finds a Sanctuary, and keeps monsters off until the gate opens. This Sanctuary then acts as a player hub where gold can be spent on upgrades and progress into other maps for story, more gold, and more level-ups. 

It's very much a standard horde survivor where leveling up grants you a choice between two perks, and by level 10-15 you are mowing through the enemies, although right now the difficulty is pleasantly surprising even at later levels.

There are four classes (Knight, Ranger, Elementalist, Necromancer) each with a unique mechanic, a skill and an ultimate ability, and they can all be maxed out on one run as the Sanctuary upgrades affect all created characters.

The game has three bosses, they are moderately challenging, and four biomes (Forest, Crypts, Sunken Crypt and the Far Shore so far), over 40 perks per class, about 20 Sanctuary upgrades from increased gold to upgraded abilities, and a fun little story where you are mistakenly thought to be the new Sanctuary Keeper by the old one, who happily crumbles to dust upon seeing you arrive.

I'm yapping too much. Point is: I feel like a child, and the fact that the video didn't come out as complete gibberish and spaghetti-eating Will Smith made my night.
